slots.title: Malcolm's composition untouched; liquid and label corrected
slots.prompt: Take the first reference photograph and keep the woman exactly as she is: the same over-the-shoulder pose looking back into the lens, the same face and expression, the same dark hair swept up, the same bare shoulder across the lower frame, the same deep graphite backdrop, the same lighting, and the same framing with the bottle held up at the right and clear of her face. Do not re-pose her, do not re-light her, do not move the hand or the bottle, and do not smooth her skin - keep its real pores, fine lines and freckles, with no allover swirl or repeating pattern anywhere. Replace the bottle with the exact bottle in the second reference image: a 30ml FROSTED COLOURLESS glass dropper bottle, straight-sided with softly rounded shoulders, fitted with a tall brushed silver aluminium collar and a translucent white rubber-bulb pipette. The glass is frosted and colourless - it has no colour of its own. Inside it the serum is a CLEAR, COLOURLESS, WATER-TRANSPARENT liquid and must read as a liquid rather than as a solid fill: the glass pipette stem is visible standing in it, there is a faint meniscus at the fill line near the top of the bottle, and the air space above that line is visibly empty. The contents are never white, milky, creamy, opaque or pearlescent. Reproduce the front label exactly as in the second reference, every character verbatim, in this order, with these weights: the Skingenetix DNA double-helix mark in black at the top, the wordmark 'Skingenetix' in bold black beneath it, then a thin vertical silver rule down the left of the text block, and beside that rule 'ACETYL' and 'HEXAPEPTIDE-8' in bold black capitals on two lines, 'ANTI-WRINKLE' and 'SERUM' in mid-grey capitals on two lines, 'PREMIUM FORMULA' in plain black capitals, and at the foot '10% ACETYL HEXAPEPTIDE-8 | 30ML' in small black capitals. Do not add, remove, reorder or restyle any word. The label is turned square to camera, is the plane of focus and the sharpest thing in the picture, every character crisply edged and legible at full resolution down to the smallest line, with enough contrast against the frosted glass that the grey lines read as clearly as the black ones. Her fingers stay clear of the lettering.
